h: The Shabbat Meals and the Divine Presence
The language of the holy meals expresses the distinct spiritual illuminations of Shabbat and Yom Tov.
The Distinct Mysteries of the Shabbat Meals

p: בְּיוֹם טוֹב אוֹמְרִים: "דָּא הוּא סְעוֹדָתָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ",
— On Yom Tov we recite: "This is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,"
וּבְשַׁבָּת אוֹמְרִים: "סְעוֹדָתָא דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין וּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין",
— while on Shabbat we recite: "The meal of the Field of Holy Apples and Ze'eir Anpin,"
שֶׁהוּא עִנְיָן אֶחָד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ:
— which are essentially one and the same theme as the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah:
קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּחִינַת זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין,
— the Holy One, blessed be He, being the aspect of Ze'eir Anpin,
וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ הוּא חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין.
— and His Shechinah being the Field of Holy Apples.
אַךְ נוֹסָף בְּשַׁבָּת סְעוֹדָתָא דְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא.
— Yet there is added on Shabbat the meal of Atika Kadisha.
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה נִשְׁתַּנָּה הַלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁל שְׁתֵּי הַסְּעוּדוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
— And we must understand why the phrasing of the two meals on Shabbat changed
מִלָּשׁוֹן הַנֶּאֱמָר בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
— from the phrasing uttered on Yom Tov,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם עִנְיָן אֶחָד?
— inasmuch as they represent one identical concept?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא,
— However, the matter is,
כִּי בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא הוּא הַהִתְקַשְׁרוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— that the aspect of Atik is the bond that Israel possesses with Hashem, blessed be He,
לְמַעְלָה מִן הַדַּעַת וּתְפִיסַת אָדָם,
— transcending mortal intellect and human comprehension;
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת קַרְקַפְתָּא דִּתְפִלִּין לְמַעְלָה מִן הַמּוֹחִין,
— and this corresponds to the crown of the head of tefillin, above the intellectual faculties,
וְכָתוּב בָּהֶם: "ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה' אֶחָד",
— within which is written: "Hashem our God, Hashem is One";
וּבִתְפִלִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא כְּתִיב: "מִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד".
— and within the tefillin of the Master of the World it is written: "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation".
וְעַל הִתְקַשְׁרוּת הַזֶּה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי ה' יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלֶךָ",
— And concerning this supernal bond it is stated: "For Hashem shall be your confidence (be-khislekha),"
וּכִדְאִיתָא בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי: "בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁאַתָּה כְּסִיל בָּהֶם",
— as brought in the Yerushalmi: "In matters wherein you are foolish/ignorant (kesil),"
הַיְינוּ אֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ תְּפִיסַת הָאָדָם
— meaning even in a realm where man holds no comprehension,
שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַהַשָּׂגָה;
— which lies completely above cognitive grasp;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְקַיֵּים בְּיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
— and as was fulfilled in our father Isaac, peace be upon him,
כְּשֶׁרָצָה לְבָרֵךְ אֶת עֵשָׂו עַל פִּי תְּפִיסַת שִׂכְלוֹ,
— when he sought to bless Esau according to his intellectual evaluation,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה נִזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לַבְּרָכָה עַל יְדֵי הַסְּעוּדָה
— and nonetheless there was brought before him the one who was truly worthy of the blessing through the meal,
דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ: "וָאֹכַל מִכֹּל",
— concerning which it is written: "And I ate of everything,"
וְנִדְרַשׁ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה): "מִכָּל טוּב שֶׁמְּתוּקָן לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא".
— and expounded in Bereishit Rabbah: "From all the goodness prepared for the righteous in the World to Come."
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הוֹפִיעַ בּוֹ בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא
— And through this there radiated within him the aspect of Atika
מֵהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם.
— from the primordial Root that transcends human comprehension.
וּקְדוּשַׁת מִדָּה זוֹ נִשְׁפָּע גַּם כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת לְנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— And the holiness of this attribute is likewise bestowed on Shabbat unto the souls of Israel,
הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם,
— the Source that transcends human perception,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "לָדַעַת כִּי אֲנִי ה' מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם",
— as it is said: "To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
וּבְחִינָה זוֹ נִקְרָא אֲרִיךְ אַנְפִּין,
— and this dimension is termed Arikh Anpin,
וּכְמַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה כז):
— and as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of Parashah 27):
"גָּדוֹל כֹּחָן שֶׁל נְבִיאִים שֶׁמְּדַמִּין צוּרָה לְיוֹצְרָהּ וְכוּלֵי,
— "Great is the power of the prophets who compare the form to its Creator, etc.,
וְעַל דְּמוּת הַכִּסֵּא דְּמוּת כְּמַרְאֵה אָדָם וְגוֹמֵר".
— and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man, etc."
וְהַשְׁפָּעַת קְדוּשָּׁה מִלְּעֵילָא שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אֵיזֶה תְּפִיסָה מִצַּד הַשֵּׂכֶל,
— And the bestowal of holiness from Above wherein there is some intellectual grasp
נִקְרָא נֶגֶד בְּחִינָה רִאשׁוֹנָה זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין.
— is termed, relative to that first higher dimension, Ze'eir Anpin.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
— In contrast to Yom Tov,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַשְׁפָּעַת קְדוּשָּׁה מִלְּעֵילָא בִּכְלָל בְּשֵׁם קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
— where the influx of holiness from Above in general is termed the Holy One, blessed be He;
וּלְזֶה גַּם כֵּן נִשְׁתַּנָּה הַשֵּׁם שְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ שֶׁבְּיוֹם טוֹב,
— and for this reason the name 'Shechinteih' used on Yom Tov was also changed [on Shabbat],
שֶׁהוּא הָאִתְעָרוּתָא מִצַּד נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— which represents the awakening from the side of the souls of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲנִי ה' שֹׁכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל",
— as it is said: "I am Hashem Who dwells in the midst of the children of Israel,"
וְהַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— namely the dimension of Knesset Yisrael.
וּבְשַׁבָּת, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ הַשְׁפָּעָה עֶלְיוֹנָה מִלְּמַעְלָה,
— And on Shabbat, because there exists a supreme influx from Above,
דְּהַיְינוּ מִטַּלָּא דִּנְטִיף מֵעַתִּיקָא,
— namely from the supernal dew that drips from Atika,
נִקְרֵאת קְדוּשַׁת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשֵׁם חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין,
— the holiness of Knesset Yisrael is designated by the name Field of Holy Apples,
הַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת שָׂדֶה שֶׁהִיא מַזְרַעַת וְהוֹלִידָה וְהִצְמִיחָה
— meaning the dimension of a field that is seeded, bears fruit, and blossoms
עַל יְדֵי הַטַּלָּא דִּנְטִיף מֵעַתִּיקָא,
— through the dew that drips from Atika,
וְאַטִּיל לַחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין
— and casts forth into the Field of Holy Apples,
לְנַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ תַּפּוּחִין.
— unto the souls of Israel who are termed apples.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 67:2: ““Isaac was overcome with great trembling” – Rabbi Ḥama ben Rabbi Ḥanina said: “Great” – more than the trembling that he trembled atop the altar. He said: “Who [then], is” the one who became an intermediary between me and the Omnipresent so that Jacob would receive the blessings? He said it regarding Rebecca. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who has two sons, one leaving and one entering, trembles? I wonder. It is, rather, that when Esau entered to his father, Gehenna entered with him. Rabbi Aḥa said: The walls of the house began seething. That is what is written: “Who then [mi efo],” who is that who is destined to be baked here, is it me, or my son Jacob? The Holy One blessed be He said to him: ‘It is neither you nor your son, but rather, “he who hunted game.”’ “He who hunted game” – Rabbi Elazar bar Shimon said: Hunter, how did they trap you? Conqueror of gates, how are your gates conquered and ruined? That is what is written: “The deceitful will not scorch [yaḥarokh] his prey” (Proverbs 12:27). The Rabbis say: The Holy One blessed be He does not delay [yeaḥer] and does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit. Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Yosei said: What is “will not scorch [lo yaḥarokh]”? the Holy One Blessed be He does not extend [yaarikh] for the deceitful one and his deceit, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: That entire day, Esau was trapping gazelles and binding them, and an angel came and untied them, [trapping] birds, and tied their wings, and an angel would come and free them. Why to that extent? “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious” (Proverbs 12:27) – so that Jacob, who was the glory of [yekaro] the world, would come and take the blessings, as from the outset of the world they were designated [ḥarutzot] for him. Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa asked Rabbi Aḥa, he said to him: ‘What is what is written: “But the wealth of a worthy [yakar] man is precious [ḥarutz]”?’ He said: ‘It is designated [ḥarutza] in the hands of the righteous, who do not receive in this world any of the glory they have coming to them in the World to Come.’ “And I ate from all [mikol]” – Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: Of everything [mikol] that was created during the six days of Creation. Rabbi Neḥemya says: Of all [mikol] the goodness that is reserved for the World to Come. He [Esau] said to him [Isaac]: ‘What was the main course that he fed you?’ He said to him: ‘I do not know, but I tasted the taste of bread, the taste of meat, the taste of fish, the taste of grasshoppers, the taste of all the delicacies of the world.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: When he [Isaac] mentioned meat, he [Esau] immediately cried. He said: ‘He fed me one bowl of lentils and took my birthright. You, to whom he fed meat, all the more so.’ Rabbi Levi said: Because our patriarch Isaac was afraid and saying: ‘Did I, perhaps, not act properly, in that I rendered one who was not firstborn, firstborn?’ When he said: “He took my birthright” (Genesis 27:36), he said: ‘I gave the blessing properly.’ Rabbi Elazar said: Ratification of a document is only by its signatories, so that you will not say that had Jacob not deceived Isaac, he would not have received the blessings. The verse states: “Indeed, he shall be blessed.””

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 27:1: ““The Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day” (Genesis 6:5). “The Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great” – it is written: “For there is a man whose work is with wisdom, with knowledge, and with smoothness” (Ecclesiastes 2:21). Rabbi Yudan said: How great is the power of prophets, in that they can liken the creation to its Creator, as it is stated, [describing a vision of God]: “I heard the voice of a man by the Ulai” (Daniel 8:16). Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said: You have another verse that is even clearer than this one, as it is stated [describing a vision of God]: “And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness, like the appearance of a man” (Ezekiel 1:26). “Whose work is with wisdom” – as it is stated: “The Lord founded the earth with wisdom” (Proverbs 3:19). “With knowledge” – as it is stated: “With His knowledge the depths were breached” (Proverbs 3:20). “And with smoothness” – Rabbi Berekhya in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon: Neither with toil nor with exertion did the Holy One blessed be He create His world, but rather, “With the word of the Lord the heavens were made” (Psalms 33:6) – upon [utterance of] the word of the Lord, the heavens were already made. “But he will give it over to a man who did not toil for it to be his portion” (Ecclesiastes 2:21) – this is the generation of the Flood. “This too is futility and a great evil” (Ecclesiastes 2:21) – “the Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great.””

paragraphs.text: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 12:1: “The matter of the three Shabbat meals: the essence of Shabbat is the daytime meal of Atika Kadisha, the Holy Ancient One, as is known from the Zohar, Beshalach, and Sifra di-Tzeniuta concerning “Why do you cry out to Me?”—it depends upon Atika, for human effort does not reach there at all. Shabbat, likewise, is cessation and the absence of effort, being a likeness of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b), which is not the world of action. Rather, its holiness is fixed and enduring (Pesachim 117b), and does not come through human effort or through Israel’s sanctifying it. It is therefore called a “good gift” (Shabbat 10b), since it does not come through effort.
